templates.default: Off-field incident
A first report has reached you about {subject}. Little is confirmed, and the first account may be worse or milder than the facts.

variants.text: Campus police and the school have been in touch about {subject}. The first account is partial; the school may act before you do.
A call came in the night about {subject}. The first report is partial and the club has not yet confirmed anything.

templates.default: The facts about {subject} are in. Reporters have the story and are asking {team} for a response.

variants.text: The facts about {subject} are in. The athletic director has been told and reporters are asking the program for a response.
The facts about {subject} are in. The owner has been told and reporters are asking {team} for a response.

templates.default: An outside process on {subject} is under way. It runs on its own clock and not yours.

variants.text: The school conduct process on {subject} is under way and the school mandatory minimums come first.
The league has taken up the case on {subject}. Its discipline replaces any club action for the same act.

templates.default: The outcome on {subject} is decided. What you did through it is on record.
League suspension
The league has suspended {subject} for {games|# game|# games}. You had no say, and the depth chart now has a gap.
{subject} has filed an appeal. The length could change before it is served.
{subject} is serving the suspension. The club facility rules for the second half of a suspension apply.
{subject} is eligible to return. His room has been waiting to see what his job looks like now.
Injury to a star
{subject} is out for the season. The plan leaned on him, and the medical staff have the timeline.
The roles around {subject} have to be reset. The room is watching who moves up.
The goals for the season may need resetting.

variants.text: The goals for the season may need resetting, and the athletic director will ask where you stand.
The goals for the season may need resetting, and the owner will ask where you stand.

templates.default: Losing streak
{team} have lost {n|# game|# games} in a row, more than preseason expectation allowed for. The film is the place to tell bad play from bad luck.
The streak is now the story around {team}. Pressure is reaching upstairs.

variants.text: The streak is now the story around {team}. The athletic director and donors are asking questions.
The streak is now the story around {team}. The owner and the general manager are asking questions.

templates.default: The streak is over. The record keeps what you changed and what you left alone, and does not credit either.
Public dispute
A dispute involving {subject} and {other} was seen in public. It was about football, and cameras or reporters were there.
The two sides of the {topic} dispute are yours to hear. Your answer will be watched more closely than the argument.
The {topic} dispute is over for now. What you did is in the record.
Hazing
Someone close to the room reports that veterans are mistreating younger players in the {room} room.
Hazing in the {room} room has surfaced: {n|# person|# people} saw it, and {subject} is named.

variants.text: Hazing in the {room} room has surfaced: {n|# person|# people} saw it, and {subject} is named. The school may require you to report it.
Hazing in the {room} room has surfaced: {n|# person|# people} saw it, and {subject} is named.

templates.default: The way you treat {subject} will be compared with how others were treated before, and everyone in the room knows the comparison.
The hazing case is closed. A hidden case would carry a later chance of coming out.
Holdout
{subject} is not practising over his contract. If he returned today the staff think he would be about {n} percent ready.
Talks on {subject} continue between the front office and his agent. The opener is {days|# day|# days} away.
The holdout is over: {subject} is back, or has been traded.
Family emergency
{subject} has come to you with a family emergency and needs to leave.
{subject} is away. Here is who would play or cover in his place, and nothing on this screen puts a price on being kind.
{subject} is back when he chose to be. What the team knows is limited to what he approved.
Team illness
The medical staff believe illness is spreading in the {room} room.
{n|# player is|# players are} out with illness. Everyone out is listed with that word and nothing more.
The illness has run its course. Everyone is back or listed.
Staff crisis
{subject} cannot work this week. {n|# task needs|# tasks need} someone to take it, starting with {task}.

variants.text: {subject} is out of the staff room this week. {n|# task needs|# tasks need} someone to take it, starting with {task}.
{subject} is out of the building this week. {n|# task needs|# tasks need} someone to take it, starting with {task}.

templates.default: Every task of {subject} has a person assigned or an uncovered mark. Taking one yourself shows the hours.
The staff crisis around {subject} is settled.
Portal exodus
Your staff think {n|# player|# players} may leave when the transfer window opens. Each read gives what it rests on, and it can be wrong.
{n|# more player has|# more players have} entered the transfer window. The list is building over the days.
The window has closed. The roster has {n|# gap|# gaps} to fill.
Academic ineligibility
Academic support reports {subject} is trending below the line.
{subject} has been ruled academically ineligible. The depth chart has a gap.
{subject} has regained eligibility.
Investigation
The school has received notice of an investigation into the program.
Interviews are under way. Recruits and their families are asking about it.
A finding has been issued. Penalties follow the infractions table.
The appeal period has begun.
Booster revolt
Donors have turned on the program. They cannot fire you, but they are making the athletic director's year hard.
The donors want {task}. Giving it to them has a price in the building.
The donor pressure has eased. Results ended it faster than anything you could do or tell them.
The boss is fired
The head coach is out. {subject} will run the building for now.
The new head coach has not named who he is keeping. Jobs are filling in the usual order.
You know where you stand: kept, passed over, or free to go to market.
Something you witnessed
You saw something involving {subject}. Only you know how sure you are, and who else may have seen it.
You can say nothing, raise it with {subject}, tell your boss, go over your boss, or go outside. No outcome is shown.
What you did is a dated fact on your history. Later employers will read it by their own profiles.
